corrections_after_observed_failures: The first sole trajectory advanced its playback clock before the shoe reached the ball. Preparation now waits for the actual weighted-skin contact before scheduling traction, with bounded gradual calibration of the shoe target.

The initial return path could cut a heel through the sphere. Return now lifts first, moves horizontally with clearance, then lowers to the planted pose. A unilateral sphere/shoe constraint solves the contacting leg against the real skinned surface, leaving the ball position unchanged.
Traction uses the measured final ankle velocity after contact projection, not the unfulfilled trajectory target velocity. Its skin acceptance remains 2.5 mm, with penetration bounded to 1 mm.

The mode holds neutral while RT remains held near the ball, but queued actions, RB sprint, incoming receptions and lost reach keep their native path. A pass can interrupt preparation after safe foot return, or fire while RT remains held after completion. Body bracing follows filtered foot height to avoid a phase jump during interruption. The test measures the planted-support/root during the held mode, separately from native approach assistance after release.
The physical-profile control regression now expects RT sole work at low speed and unchanged RB sprint. The approved nonphysical profile retains the original reserved-RT behavior.

Upper-body target limits were deliberately expanded for the requested lateral and airborne expression: pitch 0.36 rad, roll 0.20 rad, twist 0.48 rad and shoulder offset 0.48 rad, while preserving the 2.1 rad/s filter cap, native roots/legs and final anatomical limits.

The 0.68 m/s contact lift increased the sampled dribble peak by only 2.8 mm in the counterfactual comparison. The final shipped configuration uses 0.82 m/s and repeats the same on/off comparison without changing gravity, cadence or the native horizontal control.
The aerial profile audit excludes authored source contacts below 0.45 m. Source/profile counts are conditional candidates, not a full Cartesian product or captured performances.

limitations: 1000 records are 999 contextual procedural profiles and one neutral record over existing native clips. No new captured or reconstructed motion dataset was imported.
The sole gestures are a slow close-control prototype from a low-speed, nearby-ball stance. Hold RT with a direction or neutral; release/repress for another gesture. RB keeps native sprint.

Rendered tests use Linux/X11 and a virtual Xbox controller. Windows x64 was cross-compiled and its actual portable package validated; Windows GUI and physical Xbox hardware execution were unavailable.

Motion matching remains constrained by native clip, timing and ball reach feasibility. Balance is animation-guided with limited physical motors, not a learned muscular policy or Rockstar proprietary engine.
Each articulated actor has a local Bullet floor. Player interactions combine native collisions, reciprocal impulses and bounded shirt traction. Cloth and collision volumes remain approximations.
Catalog metadata candidates have not been exhaustively rendered; independent profiles and parameter contexts are not independent authored animation captures.
